Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET601 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Heinrich's Triangle Ratio: 1 Major Injury : 29 Minor Injuries : 300 Near Misses (Unsafe Acts/Conditions)
  • Heinrich's Domino Theory: Social Environment -> Fault of Person -> Unsafe Act/Condition -> Accident -> Injury
  • Accident Severity Rate (ASR): $ASR = \frac{\text{Total Days Lost} \times 10^6}{\text{Total Man-Hours Worked}}$
  • Accident Frequency Rate (AFR): $AFR = \frac{\text{Total Disabling Injuries} \times 10^6}{\text{Total Man-Hours Worked}}$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Direct vs Indirect Costs: Direct: medical bills, workers' compensation; Indirect (Iceberg theory, 4-10x higher): lost production, machine damage, retraining, legal fees.
  • Unsafe Acts vs Conditions: 88% of accidents caused by unsafe acts of persons; 10% by mechanical/physical unsafe conditions; 2% unavoidable act of god.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Removing the middle domino (Unsafe Act / Unsafe Condition) breaks the chain and prevents the injury.
  • Near-miss reporting is the most powerful leading indicator of industrial safety performance.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Industrial Safety Management & Loss Prevention

1. Modern Accident Causation & Loss Prevention Frameworks

Workplace accidents represent systemic failures in organizational safety climate, task design, and engineering controls. Heinrich, Bird, and Reason's Swiss Cheese model demonstrate how multiple defensive barriers must fail simultaneously for catastrophic incidents to occur.

$$F = \frac{N \times 10^6}{H}, \quad S = \frac{D \times 10^6}{H}, \quad \text{FSI} = \sqrt{\frac{F \times S}{1000}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Heavy manufacturing assembly lines, petrochemical refineries, and construction megaprojects.

Module 2.title: Safety Administration, JSA & Audit Inspection
Module 2.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 500 130" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;"><text x="20" y="25" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Job Safety Analysis (JSA) 4-Step Cycle</text><text x='70' y='75' fill='#fcd34d' font-size='13'>Job Selection → Step Breakdown → Hazard Identification → Control Measures</text></svg>
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET601 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Job Safety Analysis (JSA): Systematic breakdown of job steps to identify hazards and specify preventive controls.
  • Hierarchy of Hazard Controls: Elimination -> Substitution -> Engineering Controls -> Administrative Controls -> Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
  • Permit to Work (PTW): Mandatory formal written authorization for hazardous activities (Hot work, Confined space, Working at height, Electrical lockout).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Safety Officer Statutory Role: Advises management on compliance with Factories Act 1948, investigates incidents, conducts emergency drills.
  • Lockout/Tagout (LOTO): Isolating hazardous energy sources (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic) before maintenance using designated padlocks.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • PPE is always the LAST line of defense; engineering controls must always be prioritized.
  • Safety audits systematically verify proactive compliance against ISO 45001 occupational health standards.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Safety Administration & Hazard Mitigation

1. Systematic Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA)

JSA breaks down complex maintenance tasks into discrete job steps, systematically analyzing chemical, physical, and biomechanical risks to institute fail-safe safeguards.

$$\text{Risk Score} = \text{Severity} \times \text{Likelihood} \times \text{Exposure}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Preventative overhaul of steam turbines, chemical tank cleaning, and electrical switchyard maintenance.

Module 3.title: Safe Working Conditions: Electrical, Illumination & Noise
Module 3.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 500 130" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;"><text x="20" y="25" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Occupational Noise Exposure Limit (OSHA)</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#ef4444' font-size='14'>Max 85 dBA for 8 Hours • 3 dB Exchange Rate Halves Time</text></svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET601 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Permissible Noise Exposure: 85 dBA for 8 hours (OSHA / Indian Factories Act standard); every 3 dB increase halves allowable exposure time.
  • Sound Pressure Level ($L_p$): $L_p = 20 \log_{10}\left(\frac{p}{p_0}\right)$ dB (where $p_0 = 20$ $\mu$Pa threshold of hearing)
  • Illumination Levels (Lux): General engineering shop floor: 200-300 Lux; Precision inspection: 750-1000 Lux.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Electric Shock Severity: Determined by current magnitude, path through body, and contact duration; 10-20 mA causes muscle paralysis ('let-go' threshold); 100 mA triggers fatal ventricular fibrillation.
  • Color Coding (IS 9457): Red (Fire protection / Stop), Yellow (Caution / Radiation), Green (Safety / First aid), Blue (Mandatory instructions).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Ear muffs provide higher Noise Reduction Rating (NRR 25-30 dB) than standard foam earplugs.
  • Use double-insulated or 24V extra-low voltage tools inside confined metallic spaces.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Industrial Environmental Engineering & Safety

1. Ergonomic Lighting, Noise Control & Electrical Protection

Industrial hygiene standards dictate acceptable environmental exposure thresholds to prevent chronic occupational diseases (noise-induced hearing loss NIHL, eyestrain).

$$L_{\text{combined}} = 10 \log_{10} \left( \sum_{i=1}^n 10^{L_i / 10} \right) \text{ dB}, \quad D = \sum \frac{C_i}{T_i} \le 1.0$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Automated press shops, diesel engine test cells, and precision instrument calibration cleanrooms.

Module 4.title: Industrial Hygiene, Exposure Limits & Toxicology
Module 4.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 500 130" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;"><text x="20" y="25" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Threshold Limit Values (TLV-TWA vs STEL)</text><text x='90' y='75' fill='#10b981' font-size='13'>TLV-TWA (8 hr day, 40 hr week) • STEL (15 min peak) • Ceiling (Absolute max)</text></svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET601 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Threshold Limit Value - TWA: TLV-TWA: Time-Weighted Average concentration for conventional 8-hr workday and 40-hr workweek without adverse effect.
  • Short Term Exposure Limit (STEL): 15-minute TWA exposure which should not be exceeded at any time during a workday.
  • Ceiling Limit ($C$): Concentration that should never be exceeded even instantaneously.
  • Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS): Standard 16-section document covering chemical hazards, handling, first aid, and toxicological properties.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Exposure Routes: Inhalation (most common & fastest), Skin absorption, Ingestion, Injection.
  • Respiratory Protection: Air-purifying respirators (particulate N95, cartridge for organic vapors); Air-supplying SCBA for oxygen-deficient atmospheres ($< 19.5\% O_2$).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Never enter a confined space with oxygen content below 19.5% without continuous gas testing and standby attendant.
  • Silicosis and asbestosis are irreversible fibrotic lung diseases requiring strict engineering dust extraction at source.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Occupational Toxicology & Respiratory Protection

1. Dose-Response Dynamics & Airborne Contaminant Control

Industrial toxic chemicals follow dose-response relationships quantified by $LD_{50}$ and $LC_{50}$. Local Exhaust Ventilation (LEV) captures airborne particulates at emission point before entering worker breathing zones.

$$C_{\text{TWA}} = \frac{\sum C_i t_i}{8 \text{ hrs}}, \quad Q = V A = 1.4 P D v_c \quad (\text{LEV Hood Design})$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Chemical paint spray booths, battery manufacturing lead handling, and pharmaceutical bulk drug reactors.

Module 5.title: Fire Protection & Pressure Vessel Safety Regulations
Module 5.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 500 130" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;"><text x="20" y="25" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Fire Tetrahedron & Pressure Relief Protection</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#ef4444' font-size='14'>Fuel + Oxygen + Heat + Uninhibited Chemical Chain Reaction</text></svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET601 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Fire Tetrahedron: Fuel + Oxygen + Heat + Uninhibited Chemical Chain Reaction (Removing any one extinguishes fire).
  • Indian Boiler Regulations (IBR 1950): Mandates minimum two independent safety valves, two water level indicators, and certified hydrostatic testing at 1.5× design pressure.
  • BLEVE: Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapour Explosion (Catastrophic rupture of pressurized liquefied gas vessel under external fire exposure).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Fire Extinguisher Selection: Class A (Water/Foam), Class B (Dry Chemical Powder/CO2), Class C (CO2/Clean agent), Class D (Special dry powder for metals).
  • Rupture Disc vs Relief Valve: Rupture disc provides instantaneous non-reclosing overpressure burst protection; PRV reseats automatically.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Water should NEVER be applied to Class B flammable liquid fires or energized Class C electrical fires.
  • Pressure vessel safety relief valves must be calibrated and tested annually under SMPV (Static & Mobile Pressure Vessels) rules.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Fire Safety Dynamics & Boiler Regulations

1. Combustion Thermodynamics & Overpressure Relief

Flammable vapors ignite only within Lower and Upper Explosive Limits (LEL-UEL). Sizing pressure safety relief valves (PSV) under ASME Section VIII prevents catastrophic vessel burst.

$$A = \frac{W}{C K_d P_1} \sqrt{\frac{T Z}{M}} \quad (\text{API 520 Safety Valve Orifice Sizing})$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: LPG/LNG storage bottling terminals, high pressure steam boilers, and refinery fractionation columns.
